questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. This keeps you and others safe. Before moving your vehicle, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt. Secure any loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: If your vehicle has airbags, should you still wear your seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together to protect you in a crash. Always wear your lap and shoulder belts, even if your vehicle has airbags.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they contradict traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a road with a solid yellow line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken yellow line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken yellow line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Who can park in handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
Anyone, but only if all other spaces are full.
People who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
questions.explanation: You must have a handicap license plate or hanging tag to park in a handicap space. These are reserved for people with disabilities.

questions.question: What can reduce your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee and food do not help.

questions.question: Before you turn on the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your belt and check that all passengers are buckled in.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A person with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until they cross.
Wait until they cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until they cross the street.
questions.explanation: People with guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way. Always wait for them to cross.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive if you took medication that impairs your driving?

options.text: Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Do not drive if any medication makes you drowsy or impairs your driving. This includes prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Must you obey school crossing guards?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, at all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let time pass.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Fresh air, coffee, showers, and exercise will not help.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee and showers do not speed up this process.

questions.question: When you enter a main road from a private driveway, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to traffic already on the road.
Honk to make other drivers move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already on the road.
questions.explanation: When entering a main road from a private driveway, yield to all traffic. Also yield to pedestrians on any sidewalk.

questions.question: Why should you give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are harder to see and react unpredictably. Watch for them near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Watch for kids on bikes who may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check for traffic behind and beside your vehicle. Make sure the lane is clear before you move into it.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads make your tires grip less. You should slow down when the road is wet or icy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road. If you see it, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around and do not drive forward.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phones take your hands, eyes, and mind off the road. Using one while driving increases your crash risk, even if you are a skilled driver.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean you cannot pass other vehicles. These areas have limited visibility and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing, it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing. Never pass a bus when it is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reaction time and dulls your thinking. Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement causes slippery conditions. Slow down when you see this sign because it takes longer to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch all around—beside, ahead, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch all around—beside, ahead, and behind.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your car—beside, ahead, and behind. Good drivers know what is happening everywhere around their vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol may affect a driver's:
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment and coordination. Driving with any alcohol in your system is unsafe and can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a pedestrian crossing. When you see it, be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other cars from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating frustrates other drivers and can lead to aggressive driving. You can receive a traffic citation for unsafe driving.

questions.question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving. They are especially dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: Before returning to your lane after passing, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your lane after you see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror. This means you have enough distance to safely move over.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked. You must stop for them.
